1.title: Helm and Kustomize
1.text: Welcome to Module six: Helm and Kustomize. It covers the exam area Application Deployment. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Use the Helm package manager to deploy existing packages. Kustomize. Practice with eight hands-on labs worth fifty-three points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Application Deployment (twenty percent). Practice in this module: eight labs, fifty-three points, about fifty-seven minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: Two ways to avoid copying YAML
1.text: Two ways to avoid copying yamel. The figure shows this: Helm and Kustomize side by side. Exam tip: Choose Helm to install a packaged chart or roll it back, and Kustomize to patch your own yamel for each environment.

1.title: Two ways to avoid copying YAML, continued
1.text: Two ways to avoid copying yamel. Idea. Helm: a package (chart) with templates, filled in with values. Kustomize: plain yamel base plus overlays that patch it. Result. Helm: a release that Helm tracks (history, upgrade, rollback). Kustomize: ordinary objects, applied with kube control apply dash k. Typical use. Helm: install software someone else packaged. Kustomize: one app, several environments (dev, staging, prod). On the exam. Helm: docs allowed: helm dot S H or docs. Kustomize: docs allowed: Kubernetes dot I O (customize pages).

1.title: Helm in one page
1.text: Helm in one page. A chart is a folder (or a dot tgz ) with Chart dot yaml, values dot yaml (the defaults) and templates or. A repository is a web server with an index dot yaml listing charts. A release is one installation of a chart in a namespace, with a name. Exam tip: Always pass dash n namespace to Helm commands, and verify with helm list dash n namespace.

1.title: Helm in one page, continued
1.text: Helm in one page. Add a repository. helm repo add local H T T P colon slash slash one hundred twenty-seven dot zero dot zero dot one eight thousand eight hundred seventy-nine. Refresh the index. helm repo update. List repositories. helm repo list. Search a repository. helm search repo webapp ( the versions flag for every version). See the default values. helm show values local slash webapp. Install. helm install shop local slash webapp dash n helm ns the create namespace flag the version flag zero dot one dot zero. Override a value. the set flag replica Count two or the set flag service dot type Node Port. Values from a file. dash f prod values dot yaml (several dash f allowed; later ones win). Wait for readiness. the wait flag the timeout flag one hundred twenty seconds. List releases. helm list dash n helm ns ( dash A for all namespaces).

1.title: Helm in one page, continued
1.text: Helm in one page. Status of a release. helm status shop dash n helm ns. Upgrade. helm upgrade shop local slash webapp dash n helm ns the set flag replica Count three. History and rollback. helm history shop dash n helm ns, helm rollback shop one dash n helm ns. Values you supplied. helm get values shop dash n helm ns (add the all flag for defaults too). Rendered manifests of a release. helm get manifest shop dash n helm ns. Render without installing. helm template preview local slash webapp the set flag replica Count four. Remove. helm uninstall shop dash n helm ns.

1.title: Helm in one page, continued
1.text: Helm in one page. Always give dash n namespace (releases live in a namespace; without it Helm uses the current one). The Deployment of a release is usually named release - chart, for example shop webapp: read it from kube control get deploy dash n helm ns. Precedence of values (low to high): the chart's values dot yaml, then dash f files (in order), then the set flag. helm upgrade keeps nothing from the earlier install unless you pass the reuse values flag: repeat your the set flag flags or use the reuse values flag.

1.title: Helm in one page, continued
1.text: Helm in one page. Rollback creates a new revision. After install (one), upgrade (two) and rollback one, helm history shows three revisions and the last one has the description "Rollback to one". Charts from a directory. helm install shop. slash webapp installs a chart folder. helm create webapp makes a starter chart, helm lint. slash webapp checks it, helm package. slash webapp builds the dot tgz, and helm pull local slash webapp the untar flag downloads and unpacks one. Exam tip. Tasks name the release, the namespace, the chart and often a version or a value. Copy them exactly, then verify with helm list dash n ns and kube control get deploy dash n ns.

1.title: Kustomize in one page
1.text: Kustomize in one page. Kustomize reads a customization dot yaml and builds the final yamel without templates. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: kube control apply dash k dir applies a customization and kube control customize dir only previews it.

1.title: Kustomize in one page, continued
1.text: Kustomize in one page. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Kustomize in one page, continued
1.text: Kustomize in one page. Preview. kube control customize overlays slash prod (builds, prints, changes nothing). Apply. kube control apply dash k overlays slash prod. Delete. kube control delete dash k overlays slash prod. Add a Config Map. config Map Generator with literals or files; the name gets a hash suffix, and references in Pods are rewritten for you. Add a Secret. secret Generator. Change one field. patches with target and a patch: Jason patch ( op add slash replace slash remove ) or a strategic merge snippet. Change an image. images ( name, new Name, new Tag ). Shared annotations. common Annotations.

1.title: Kustomize in one page, continued
1.text: Kustomize in one page. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Kustomize in one page, continued
1.text: Kustomize in one page. The generated Config Map is named web config- hash; Kustomize changes the name in config Map Ref to match, and a change to the data changes the hash, which restarts the Pods. Build with kube control customize first to read errors; the usual ones are a wrong relative path in resources (.. slash base versus.. or.. slash base ), a typo in a field name, and a patch target that matches nothing. Exam tip. kube control apply dash k needs the directory that holds customization dot yaml, not the file. Never edit the base when the task says to use an overlay.

1.title: Helm or Kustomize?
1.text: Helm or Kustomize? "Install this chart or this version or with these values or roll it back": Helm. "The same app in prod with three replicas and another image": Kustomize. Both can be combined (Helm renders, Kustomize patches) but the exam keeps them separate. Exam tip: Never edit the Kustomize base when the task asks for an overlay: all changes go in the overlay.

1.title: Lab 6.1: helm repo install
1.text: Lab six point one: helm repo install. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. A Helm chart repository is served at H T T P colon slash slash one hundred twenty-seven dot zero dot zero dot one eight thousand eight hundred seventy-nine. Add it to Helm under the name local, refresh the index, and look at the available versions of the chart webapp. Install version zero dot one dot zero (not the newest) as the release shop in the namespace helm ns (create the namespace with the install), with two replicas, by overriding the chart value replica Count on the command line. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 6.1: helm repo install, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run helm repo add local H T T P colon slash slash one hundred twenty-seven dot zero dot zero dot one eight thousand eight hundred seventy-nine. Then helm repo update. Then helm search repo local slash webapp the versions flag. Then helm install shop local slash webapp the version flag zero dot one dot zero dash n helm ns the create namespace flag the set flag replica Count two the wait flag the timeout flag, and so on. Then helm list dash n helm ns. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 6.2: helm upgrade rollback
1.text: Lab six point two: helm upgrade rollback. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The release app (chart local slash webapp version zero dot one dot zero, one replica) is installed in the namespace helm ns; the repository local is already added. Upgrade the release to chart version zero dot two dot zero with three replicas. Then the upgrade turns out to be a mistake: roll the release back to its first revision. At the end the release must run chart zero dot one dot zero with one replica, and the history must show the upgrade and the rollback. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 6.2: helm upgrade rollback, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run helm upgrade app local slash webapp the version flag zero dot two dot zero dash n helm ns the set flag replica Count three the wait flag the timeout flag one hundred twenty seconds. Then helm history app dash n helm ns. Then helm rollback app one dash n helm ns the wait flag the timeout flag one hundred twenty seconds. Then helm history app dash n helm ns. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 6.3: helm values file
2.text: Lab six point three: helm values file. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The file about slash work slash prod values dot yaml holds the settings for production. Install the newest version of the chart local slash webapp (the repository local is already added) as the release site in the namespace helm ns (create it with the install), taking the values from that file. Do not edit the file. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 6.3: helm values file, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run helm show values local slash webapp then pipe to head -twenty. Then helm install site local slash webapp dash n helm ns the create namespace flag dash f about slash work slash prod values dot yaml the wait flag the timeout flag one hundred twenty seconds. Then helm get values site dash n helm ns. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 6.4: helm uninstall values
2.text: Lab six point four: helm uninstall values. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. Two releases exist in the namespace helm ns: old and keep. Remove the release old completely. Save the user-supplied values of the release keep (not the chart defaults) to the file about slash answers slash keep values dot yaml. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 6.4: helm uninstall values, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run helm list dash n helm ns. Then helm uninstall old dash n helm ns. Then helm get values keep dash n helm ns about slash answers slash keep values dot yaml. Then cat about slash answers slash keep values dot yaml. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 6.5: helm show values template
2.text: Lab six point five: helm show values template. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. Without installing anything: (one) find the default value of image dot repository in the chart local slash webapp (the repository local is already added) and write only that value to about slash answers slash repo dot txt; (two) render the manifests of the chart for a release named preview with four replicas and save the output to about slash answers slash rendered dot yaml. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 6.5: helm show values template, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run helm show values local slash webapp then pipe to grep -A three starts with image. Then echo engine X about slash answers slash repo dot txt. Then helm template preview local slash webapp the set flag replica Count four about slash answers slash rendered dot yaml. Then grep dash E replicas then pipe to name preview about slash answers slash rendered dot yaml. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 6.6: kustomize overlay
2.text: Lab six point six: customize overlay. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. A Kustomize base exists in about slash kust slash base (a Deployment web with one replica and a Service web ). Create an overlay in about slash kust slash overlays slash prod that reuses the base and changes: namespace prod, a name prefix prod-, three replicas, and the container image to engine X stable alpine. Do not edit the base. Create the namespace prod, then apply the overlay to the cluster. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 6.6: kustomize overlay, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. cat about slash kust slash overlays slash prod slash customization dot yaml. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control customize about slash kust slash overlays slash prod then pipe to head -thirty. Then kube control create ns prod. Then kube control apply dash k about slash kust slash overlays slash prod. Then kube control dash n prod rollout status deployment prod web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 6.7: kustomize config generator
2.text: Lab six point seven: customize config generator. This task is worth eight points, and you should plan about nine minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. A Kustomize base exists in about slash kust slash base (a Deployment web and a Service web ). Create an overlay in about slash kust slash overlays slash staging that reuses the base and: sets the namespace staging, generates a Config Map named web config with the literal level info, and patches the Deployment so that its container loads all keys of that Config Map as environment variables ( env From ). Do not edit the base. Create the namespace staging and apply the overlay. The running Pod must show level info in its environment. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 6.7: kustomize config generator, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. cat about slash kust slash overlays slash staging slash customization dot yaml. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 6.7: kustomize config generator, Solution, continued
2.text: Lab six point seven: customize config generator, Solution, continued. Run kube control customize about slash kust slash overlays slash staging then pipe to head -forty. Then kube control create ns staging. Then kube control apply dash k about slash kust slash overlays slash staging. Then kube control dash n staging rollout status deployment web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then kube control dash n staging exec deploy slash web then the command printenv level.

2.title: Lab 6.8: fix kustomize overlay
2.text: Lab six point eight: fix customize overlay. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-ckad context. The overlay about slash kust slash overlays slash prod fails with kube control apply dash k. Fix the overlay (do not change the base) so that it deploys the Deployment prod web (name prefix prod- ) and the Service prod web into the namespace prod, with two replicas. Create the namespace prod and apply the overlay. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 6.8: fix kustomize overlay, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control customize about slash kust slash overlays slash prod two one then pipe to head -three. Then make the edit with sed, as shown on the screen. Then kube control customize about slash kust slash overlays slash prod then pipe to head -twelve. Then kube control create ns prod. Then kube control apply dash k about slash kust slash overlays slash prod. Then kube control dash n prod rollout status deployment prod web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is a Helm release? Answer: One installation of a chart in a namespace, with a name and a history of revisions. Question two. Which command shows the default values of a chart? Answer: helm show values repo or chart. Question three. How do you install a specific chart version? Answer: helm install release repo or chart the version flag x dot y dot z.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which value source wins: a dash f file or the set flag? Answer: the set flag wins over dash f files, which win over the chart defaults. Question five. How do you see only the values you supplied to a release? Answer: helm get values release (add the all flag for the chart defaults too). Question six. How do you render a chart without installing it? Answer: helm template release chart the set flag....

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. Which command applies a Kustomize overlay, and which one only prints it? Answer: kube control apply dash k dir applies; kube control customize dir prints. Question eight. What does name Prefix do, and why does a generated Config Map name have a hash? Answer: It prefixes every object name; the hash changes when the data changes, so Pods that use the Config Map restart.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Helm repo: repo add, repo update, search repo the versions flag, show values. Helm release: install, upgrade, rollback, uninstall, list dash n, history, get values. Values: defaults less than dash f less than the set flag; the reuse values flag on upgrade. Preview: helm template, kube control customize. Kustomize: resources, namespace, name Prefix, replicas, images, patches, generators. Apply: kube control apply dash k directory. Base untouched: change things in the overlay only. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. In the next module, we continue the course.
